prompt: The parent parabola $y = x^2$ is changed to $y = x^2 + 5$. How many units UP does the graph slide?
hint: The $+5$ sits OUTSIDE the square, so it changes the $y$-value of every point.

hints.text: The $+5$ sits OUTSIDE the square, so it changes the $y$-value of every point.
Adding $5$ to every output lifts the whole sticker straight up the window.

explanation: In the form $f(x) + k$, the number $k$ is added after the function has done its job, so it changes outputs and not inputs.
Here $k = 5$, which means every $y$-value on the parabola becomes $5$ larger than before.
Raising every point by the same amount moves the whole graph straight up, so it slides UP $5$ units.

alternativeExplanations.title: Follow one point
steps: On $y = x^2$ the bottom point is $(0, 0)$.
That bottom point moved from $(0, 0)$ to $(0, 5)$ — up 5.
